findings.breaking_input: A draft whose remote load hides from the regexes: an unquoted attribute (`<script src=https://evil.example/x.js>`), a `<style>@import url(https://evil.example/a.css)</style>` is caught only by CSS_URL, but `<meta http-equiv=refresh>`, `<base href="https://evil.example/">` (base is not in LOAD_TAGS), `<form action=...>`, or an inline `style="background:url(https://evil.example/p.png)"` on a tag not in the list. LOAD_ATTRS requires quoted values, so unquoted src is missed by both the rewrite and the belt-and-braces check.
findings.why: Self-containment is declared proven by the same reader that missed the load. A page with a remaining remote load is vendored as DRAFTED and the jury renders a half-online page; the final check reuses the blind reader, so it cannot catch what it cannot see.
findings.fix: Parse with a real HTML tokenizer, accept unquoted attributes, and add base/form/meta/object. Backstop with a scan of the final HTML for any `//host` or `https?:` substring outside allowed anchors.
findings.twin_of: A pin applied to one tool and not its twin -> a check added for one tool is added to every tool that resolves the same relative path.

findings.breaking_input: Draft contains `x` or text/code mentioning the same URL string, alongside a real ``. Also a raw of `//cdn.tailwindcss.com` is a substring of other URLs.
findings.why: Global string replace of ref.raw rewrites every occurrence, including anchors and body text, not only the load attribute. Contradicts the claim that only src/href targets change, and substring raws (e.g. a short raw contained inside a longer URL) corrupt other URLs so a different host's URL is mangled into an assets/ path; the recorded rewrites are then inaccurate.
findings.fix: Rewrite by match offset inside the specific tag, with the attribute boundaries, not a global split/join.
findings.twin_of: A check on the first URL that no redirect hop repeats -> every hop passes every check the first URL passed.

findings.breaking_input: An asset whose server omits Content-Length and streams a huge body, or a 200 with chunked 2 GB. `res.arrayBuffer()` is fully buffered before the length check.
findings.why: The cap is enforced after the whole body is in memory, so a hostile or broken response exhausts memory. The same applies to `download()` for the HTML (arrayBuffer then check). MAX_TOTAL_ASSET_BYTES is also checked only after the fetch completes.
findings.fix: Stream the body with a reader, abort when the running total passes the cap, and make each fetch's deadline cover the body read.
findings.twin_of: A keyed request whose deadline, size and reply count were the server's to choose -> a deadline and a byte cap on every remote body

findings.breaking_input: The HTML URL on contribution.usercontent.google.com answers 302 to another host. `redirect:"error"` throws, but the fetch also resolves the hostname by normal DNS, with no IP check, so a host resolving to a private address is fetched.
findings.why: Host allowlist is by name only. realAsset likewise connects to allow-listed hostnames without validating the resolved address, and the htmlUrl's port is not checked (`https://contribution.usercontent.google.com:8443/`), because only hostname is compared.
findings.fix: Require u.port === "" or 443 in readAnswer and the asset allowed(); pin the resolution if DNS poisoning is in scope.
findings.twin_of: A permission check resolved the host once and the connection resolved it again

findings.breaking_input: `--run` validated as ID, but the explore dir docs/design/explore/<runId> is never checked to be the explore's real dir. design-explore.sh passes $ID while the jury reads `basename(ex.dir)`. A run like `con` is refused by RESERVED, but the explore passes through `rmSync(rivalDir,{recursive,force})` with no check that rivalDir is not a symlink or junction.
findings.why: If rival-stitch is a pre-planted symlink/junction into another directory, rmSync recursive follows or deletes through it on Windows junctions, then mkdir/write land elsewhere. Cleanup also deletes a rival dir from an earlier run of the same id even when this run never created it, e.g. a prior DRAFTED page is destroyed by a later failed attempt that reaches the vendor step.
findings.fix: lstat the dir and refuse a symlink; stage into a temp dir and rename only on success; clean up only what this run created.
findings.twin_of: Cleanup deleted a content-addressed file an earlier run owned -> clean up only what this run created.

findings.breaking_input: Run 1 DRAFTED, then run 2 with the same --run fails early (no key, bad key, quota). Receipt.json is overwritten with COULD-NOT-DRAFT, but the earlier rival-stitch/index.html remains. The jury treats the receipt as the gate, so it is left out; conversely a failed draft after a vendoring step crash leaves the receipt of the previous DRAFTED.
findings.why: The receipt and the page can disagree. A crash (exception in vendor/writeFileSync, not caught) between writing the page and settle() leaves a stale DRAFTED receipt from a prior run beside a different page, so the jury deals a page that does not match the receipt's html sha. The jury never re-hashes the page against the receipt or vendor.json.
findings.fix: Clear receipt.json and the rival dir at the start of a run; have the jury verify the page sha256 against vendor.json.
findings.twin_of: A run record that a failed begin leaves behind -> clear the record at the start of the run that will write it

findings.breaking_input: `--rival stitch` where the status.log last line for p has been forged by a tab in a provider message, or rival provider matches `.+`; plus the `rivals` path uses ex.brief and basename(ex.dir) from explore.txt, not validated. A rival name such as `a-` or one that collides with the Windows-reserved list (`con`, `nul`) passes `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and becomes a directory name.
findings.why:
The jury grammar for --rival omits the reserved-device-name half, though it becomes the path `rival-

`. design-render.sh also accepts `rival-con`/`rival-nul`.
findings.fix: Apply the RESERVED check in jury and design-render.sh, and refuse trailing `-`.
findings.twin_of: A name grammar copied without its reserved-word half -> a name that becomes a path carries both halves of the grammar, everywhere it is accepted.

findings.breaking_input: `design-explore.sh rival <id> --viewport "1440x900 --session x"`: the value is concatenated into RFLAGS and word-split unquoted into design-render.sh, so a value with spaces injects extra flags, including a second `--session`. The loop validates only that the value exists, not its shape.
findings.why: The comment claims RFLAGS is built only from validated values, but --viewport/--media values are never validated, so the unquoted $RFLAGS expansion is an argument injection (also glob expansion of `*`).
findings.fix: Validate each value against a strict grammar (`^[0-9]+x[0-9]+$`) or build a bash array and expand it quoted.
findings.twin_of: Unquoted multi-word flag value smuggles extra flags into the resolver

findings.breaking_input: The npm cache and SDK install dir are shared and persistent: a package already present at `rival-sdk/<pkg>/node_modules/@google/stitch-sdk` with a matching package.json version is trusted, though its files were never integrity-checked. Only the version string is compared. Another local process, or a poisoned previous install, replaces the entry JS.
findings.why: The child that receives STITCH_API_KEY imports whatever entry file is there. The version check is the only pin; no lockfile or hash, and `npm install --no-save` runs with transitive deps unpinned, so transitive dependencies are resolved fresh at install time.
findings.fix: Record the entry sha256 at install and verify before every run; install with a lockfile or shrinkwrap pinning transitive deps.
findings.twin_of: Test seam shipped ungated / pin applied to one tool and not its twin

findings.breaking_input: The child ignores stdin close and spawns grandchildren; `child.kill()` kills only the direct process. On the timeout the SDK may hold a socket and the parent finishes while the key-bearing child lives on, and the run dir (HOME) is rmSync'd while it is still alive.
findings.why: On Windows, killing the parent does not kill the tree, and the finally-block rmSync can fail with EBUSY while the child holds the dir, throwing out of draft with a stack trace instead of a named COULD-NOT-DRAFT line (exit 1 or crash code, not 3). The `close` event is also not awaited after kill.
findings.fix: Kill the tree (taskkill /T), wait for close, and wrap rmSync in try/catch.
findings.twin_of: A tree kill that only works while the parent lives

findings.breaking_input: Disk full or a read-only path on writeFileSync(draft.raw.html), a vendor() exception from a malformed fake-assets index, or mkdirSync(rivalDir) failing: none are inside try/catch. In a --fake-answer run, `JSON.parse` failure of the answer file is inside try, but is then rethrown by finally with no catch.
findings.why: The contract says exactly one status line and exit 3 on provider failure. An unhandled rejection from top-level await exits with code 1 and a stack trace and no status line, and exit 1 collides with the usage-error code, so the jury and the caller read a crash as a usage error.
findings.fix: Wrap the whole draft body in try/catch routed to fail(); use a verdict code the runtime never produces.
findings.twin_of: A caller read the parser's "someone else" code, 1, which is also bash's crash code

findings.breaking_input: The payload JSON is passed as argv to `bash arc-event.sh emit --payload <json>`, with `join(root,...)` as a Windows path. A root containing spaces is fine as an arg, but the MSYS bash expands `@file`-style args and the JSON begins with `{`, and on Windows `bash` may resolve to WSL (per HQ memory), where the path is not valid. The failure is only printed, and the unblind.json was already written once.
findings.why: A missing receipt is non-fatal, so the rival-beats-all-arc record can be silently absent from the spine while exit is 0; there is no timeout on the spawnSync, so a hung emit hangs unblind after the write-once file is already committed.
findings.fix: Set a timeout, treat a failed emit as a nonzero exit after writing, and pass the payload by env or a file.
findings.twin_of: A subprocess result was ignored -> read status and error of every spawn whose failure matters

findings.breaking_input: Route `docs/design/explore/x/rival-stitch/assets/../index.html`, or the case `docs/design/explore/*/rival-*/?*` where `*` crosses `/`: `docs/design/explore/a/b/rival-x/index.html` matches the first pattern with `*`=`a/b`.
findings.why: The glob lets the explore segment span slashes; the later per-part check is relied on to take it apart, but the rival branch only validates `_er_variant`, so a rival path with extra depth before it depends entirely on that later parse being right.
findings.fix: Test the segment count explicitly before the case, as the variant path has to.
findings.twin_of: A textual `..` check on a pattern language that can expand
